$comment: ROOT-GUARD OWNERSHIP MANIFEST (#1624, epic #1621).
Haven has guards that live OUTSIDE the tree they police: a lint under
scripts/ that polices packages/backend, a ratchet that polices
packages/frontend. Only the policed package's CI job actually runs them.
So a pull request that ONLY weakens such a guard -- widening an exemption
regex, deleting a refusal, loosening a rule -- would go green with the
guard never running, unless the CI change classifier is told that the
guard belongs to that job.
That knowledge used to be four bespoke arms of a case statement. It is
data now, and this file is the single place it lives. The classifier
(scripts/ci/change-classifier.mjs) turns each entry into a routing rule;
nothing else decides it.
FIELDS
path     Exact repo-root-relative path. NOT a glob -- see below.
jobs     The output flags whose CI jobs own this file. These are the
jobs that would actually catch a regression in it.
runsVia  The npm script(s) those jobs run to exercise the guard. This is
what makes `jobs` a CHECKED claim rather than an assertion:
scripts/ci/root-guard-ownership.test.mjs reads .github/workflows/ci.yml
and fails if a named job does not actually run one of these.
Two shapes (#2743): a bare name is a ROOT package.json script
(`lint:deps`); `<script> -w <workspace>` is that WORKSPACE's
(`test -w packages/sdk`), for a guard whose only real check is a
package's own suite and which therefore has no root script to
hang ownership on. Both are validated against the package.json
that must define them. Every owning job's block must contain AT
LEAST ONE entry as a whole `npm run <entry>` command -- not every
entry in every block, since frontend_checks legitimately runs
`test -w packages/frontend` and never `test -w packages/sdk`.
reason   Why this ownership, in a sentence someone can disagree with.
NOT ONLY GUARDS (#2727). An entry may also be a CANONICAL SOURCE whose
pinned copies live in other packages -- same failure shape, since the
copy's pin test runs only in the copy's own job. For such an entry
`runsVia` names a script the owning job genuinely runs, but it is not
always the whole proof: where a derivation cannot be read back, the job
is ROUTED so its own pin test runs, and `runsVia` is the routing hook
that makes the ownership expressible and checkable here.
EXACT PATHS ONLY, deliberately. The epic asks for exact paths before glob
semantics, and a guard manifest is where a too-clever glob does the most
damage: `scripts/*.mjs` would silently claim every future script in that
directory for the backend job. A new guard gets a new line. The one place
globs remain is the root-CONFIG rule in the classifier (workflow files,
package.json, tsconfig*.json), which forces the full matrix rather than
naming an owner -- a different question, and its glob behaviour is
characterized by rows in scripts/ci/routing-matrix.mjs.
ADDING A GUARD: add the entry here, and add a matrix row in
scripts/ci/routing-matrix.mjs. The tests fail until you do both -- an
entry nothing exercises is the failure mode this epic exists to remove.
NOT a completeness claim. This file says where the guards it lists belong;
it does not assert that every guard in the repo is listed. Enforcing that

guards.reason: The module-boundary rule set (#982). It is authoritative over the prose in the architecture doc, so weakening a rule here is exactly the change that must re-run the gate enforcing it.
The dependency-boundary gate itself. It scans packages/backend and packages/core but is only ever run by backend_checks.
The gate's own self-test. A lint nobody tests can start passing vacuously, so loosening the test must run it.
The shrink-only ratchet that stops the positional-mock pattern growing back in packages/backend tests (#1219).
The ratchet's self-test, for the same reason as dep-lint's: a ratchet whose test is weakened can ratchet nothing.
The shrink-only ratchet that stops the retired-rail prose phrase family growing back across packages/** (#2685). It scans all packages but only backend_checks runs it.
The ratchet's self-test, for the same reason as dep-lint's: a ratchet whose test is weakened can ratchet nothing.
Generates packages/core/src/api-types.ts from the backend OpenAPI spec. Backend rather than frontend despite writing into core: the drift check that would fail runs only in backend_checks.

The shared ratchet ENGINE, backing SIX gates as of #2747: the backend db-mock and retired-rail-prose ratchets, the frontend wire-type ratchet (#1447), the frontend copy lint, packages/frontend/scripts/design-lint, and scripts/docs/ui-gate-wording. An earlier version of this sentence said two, which is what it backed at #1447. Routing it to one job would leave the other surface's gates unguarded, which is the whole reason two jobs are named here.

The engine's own self-test, which did not exist until #2759 — six gates imported the module and each gate's suite covered only the paths that gate happens to take, so the engine's contract was tested by nobody. Both surface jobs, mirroring the engine above: a weakening reachable from either surface must run it.
The wire-type ratchet (#1447). It polices packages/frontend hooks and types, and only frontend_checks runs it.
Its self-test. Widening the exemption regex or deleting the --update refusal without running the gate is the specific failure this covers.
The network-map pin test (#1478) spans backend, SDK and signer sources, and all three jobs run it. Naming fewer would let a drift ship past the job that would have caught it.

The visual gate's honesty instrument (#2318): it names the baselines that were actually compared, and refuses an EMPTY baseline tree — the case where the pixel gate passes having compared nothing. It reads packages/frontend/e2e/__screenshots__ but lives under scripts/, and the job that reads it beside the tick (design_visual) is gated on the frontend surface, so a pull request touching only this file must be routed to frontend_checks to run it at all.
Its self-test. A report nobody tests can start answering vacuously, which is the exact defect the report exists to expose, so weakening the test must run it.

Refuses a pg_constraint lookup in packages/backend/src/db/migrations/** that is not anchored to a relation or schema (#2702). `conname` is not unique across schemas, so an unanchored lookup is answered by another schema's copy and the constraint is silently skipped — measured at 185 and 193 schemas missing three constraints. It lives under scripts/ and only backend_checks runs it, so a PR that only weakens the guard would not route to the job that runs it.

The guard's own fixtures, and they are load-bearing rather than decoration: with the repo already clean, neutering the guard's scope predicate left it GREEN (measured). These tests are the half that can go red, including a fixture in the multi-line shape a hand-written grep missed.

The canonical agent runbook, and the source of several pinned derivations that live in other packages so those packages stay installable alone. Two are FULL-TEXT copies (packages/cli/src/agent-guidance-text.ts, packages/frontend/public/for-agents.md) and lint:runbook-parity verifies both. The frontend holds two more that it cannot: src/lib/agent-onboarding-prompt.ts copies one constant, and src/lib/agent-skill-bundle.ts embeds text composed from four of them via sdk/src/skill-content.ts -- resolved text, not an extractable literal. Each derivation is byte-pinned by a test in ITS OWN package's job, and before #2727 an SDK-only change routed code, sdk, backend, connect, mcp, mcp_server and signer: neither cli nor frontend, so none of those pin tests ran. #2713 edited this file and left the CLI copy stale; the frontend copy survived only because that PR happened to touch frontend files too. dev did not even go red -- cli_checks was skipped, so the stale copy was simply carried until an unrelated backend PR (#2719) regenerated it. All three jobs are named so every pin test runs on a change here.

The generator and verifier for the runbook copies above. It lives under packages/cli/ but reads packages/sdk/, so a change here can break a check that any of the three jobs running lint:runbook-parity performs -- and these rules match before the packages/cli/* arm, so without the explicit cli in jobs a change to this file would stop routing the CLI's own suite (#2727).

The canonical generic payment skill, and the second SDK source with a cross-package pin. packages/frontend/src/lib/agent-skill-bundle.ts keeps a deliberately decoupled inline copy so the frontend deploys standalone, and packages/frontend/src/lib/__tests__/agent-skill-bundle.test.ts imports THIS file directly to assert byte-for-byte parity -- a test that runs only in frontend_checks. #2727 closed the same hole for agent-guidance.ts and left this one open (#2743): an SDK-only change here routed sdk but not frontend, so mutating a heading exited 0 on lint:runbook-parity (which reads only the two full-text runbook copies, and this is not one of them) while agent-skill-bundle.test.ts failed in a job that never ran. That copy is resolved text composed at build time, so no readable-back lint can cover it; the frontend's own suite is the check, which is why runsVia names it by workspace rather than inventing a second spelling of a check frontend_checks already runs.
